post.summary: Set the account's identity keys and recovery blob.
post.description:
Idempotent: the store coalesces, so a client that retries after a dropped
response does not get a second account. The account itself already exists by
the time this runs — it is minted when the token first resolves.

parameters.name: X-Sunrise-Device
parameters.description:
Which of the account's devices signed this request.

Renamed explicitly: the derive falls back to the field identifier
verbatim, so without this the extractor would read a header literally
named `x_sunrise_device` and describe that name to clients -- wrong on
the wire and wrong in the document, and passing every test that only
ever talks to itself.

parameters.name: X-Sunrise-Device-Sig
parameters.description: The detached Ed25519 signature, base64url no-pad.

parameters.name: Date
parameters.description: Inside the signature, so it cannot be adjusted in flight.

and the legitimate "sign out here" gesture is a local key wipe rather than a
server call.

get.summary: Stream a committed blob's ciphertext back.
get.description:
One chunk is read from disk at a time rather than the whole blob being
assembled first. The surface this replaces built a single `Vec<u8>` of up to
`MAX_BLOB_BYTES` before writing a byte, so one fetch of a large attachment
pinned 100 MB of the relay's memory for as long as the client took to read
it — and a handful of concurrent fetches was an availability problem rather
than a slow response.

parameters.description: The blob being read.

HealthResponse.description:
Health response.

`Deserialize` is here for the generated client, not for the server: spargen
reads this shape out of the document and the client decodes into it.

oidc_issuer.description:
OIDC issuer discovery URL, so an unauthenticated client can bootstrap
the login flow without static configuration. `None` in self-host mode.

oidc_client_id.description: OIDC client id tokens must be audienced to.

device_binding_mode.description:
Device-binding mode. The field exists so a client can detect a server
that has moved on without having to infer it from a 403.

device_binding_required.description:
Whether the server *requires* device binding on authenticated requests.
A client that sees `false` may still sign, and the signature is still
verified.

email.description:
User email. Normalized server-side, and only a fallback: the IdP owns
the address, and this is read solely when the verifier emits no `email`
claim at all.

identity_signing_pub.description: Identity Ed25519 public key, base64url no-pad.

identity_dh_pub.description: Identity X25519 public key, base64url no-pad.

recovery_blob.description: Encrypted recovery blob. Opaque to the server, base64url no-pad.

terms_at_ms.description: Terms acceptance timestamp, milliseconds since the epoch.

created_at_ms.description: Account creation time, milliseconds since the epoch.

AccountInfo.description: An account, as this surface reports it.

created_at_ms.description: Registration time, milliseconds since the epoch.

last_seen_at_ms.description: Last authenticated request, milliseconds since the epoch.

revoked.description:
Whether the device has been revoked.

Revocation is a soft delete: the row survives so this can be reported.

revoked_at_ms.description: Revocation time, milliseconds since the epoch.

device_pub_s.description:
Ed25519 device signing key, base64url no-pad. This is what verifies the
device's `X-Sunrise-Device-Sig` on every later request.

device_cert.description:
Self-signed device certificate. Opaque to the server, which never parses
it — trust in a device cert is established client-side by
`Command::TrustDevice`, and ADR-0024 is what gives it an identity anchor.

PushPlatform.description:
Push platform tag.

`kynos::Schema` so the typed surface can take this directly rather than a
free string: the three platforms then appear in the OpenAPI document as an
enum, and an unknown one is rejected by the parse rather than stored.

device_id.description:
Which of the caller's devices this token belongs to. Validated against
the caller's own rows; it cannot file a token under an unowned device.

platform.description:
Provider tag.

The enum rather than a free string: a token filed under a platform no
provider serves is a notification that silently never arrives, and the
parse is the cheapest place to refuse it.

token.description:
The provider token. Stored in plaintext today — see
`docs/01-architecture/threat-model.md`.

stream_id.description: Stream id this blob belongs to.

size_bytes.description:
Total ciphertext size in bytes. Advisory: the server enforces the
per-attachment ceiling here and the real size at finalize.

upload_id.description: Server-assigned upload id, used by the chunk PUTs and by `finalize`.

chunk_urls.description:
Per-chunk upload URLs. Self-host returns relative paths under
`/api/v1/blobs/<upload_id>/<idx>`, which the PUT operation serves.

content_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the concatenated chunk ciphertext, 64 lowercase hex.

chunk_hashes.description:
Per-chunk BLAKE3 hashes, 64 lowercase hex each, in order. Its length is
the chunk count: `init`'s advisory count is not trusted here.

blob_id.description:
Canonical blob id: `blb_` + the first 16 bytes of `content_hash` in
lowercase hex. Content-addressed, so re-uploading identical ciphertext
converges on the same id.

AccountToken.description: An OIDC access token for the calling account, verified against the issuer's JWKS.
